clause_evidence.clause: Solve problems involving addition and subtraction
clause_evidence.reasoning: Every one of the 23 samples presents a word problem that requires students to solve using addition and subtraction operations in various combinations. All problems are grounded in realistic contexts and directly test the student's ability to apply these operations. No sample is missing the core requirement of requiring problem-solving via addition and subtraction.

Every sample contains either 3 or 4 distinct numeric values that students must combine using addition or subtraction. Each value is clearly presented in the problem stem. All 23 samples fall within this range with no fewer than 3 and no more than 4 operands. The requirement is comprehensively met across the full sample set.

Every numeric value across all 23 samples is a number with 1 or 2 digits, ranging from single-digit values like 1 to 6, up through two-digit values from 10 to 99. No sample contains three-digit numbers or values exceeding 99. This constraint is uniformly satisfied, meeting the curriculum requirement for Grade 3 magnitude appropriateness.

The competency states problems should include those involving money. Twelve of the 23 samples explicitly involve Philippine peso currency, denoted by the peso symbol, spanning both cloze and MCQ formats. These samples represent approximately half of the total and amply demonstrate that money problems are included in the problem set. The variety of money-based scenarios meets the curricular intent to familiarize students with monetary computation.
